//: What a guard puts in a blow's way (07 §5.3). The flat of a blade, the face of a shield and the forearm each take what is left of a blow once some of it is turned aside, spread over their own area and give: a broad, yielding face spreads it thin, so a blow that the parry could not turn wholly lands on the flat at an intensity steel does not notice.
A small round shield held in the fist.
name: buckler

//: The forearm, for a block with no shield.
